ordered_diagnoses: Necrotizing fasciitis of the buccal space

facts.raw_span: a two-week history of an asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face
reduced mouth opening
two prior similar episodes over eight years
no pain or fever
a known diabetic on regular medication
gross right facial asymmetry
a 6 × 6 cm ovoid subcutaneous swelling
the borders were ill-defined, the consistency ranged from soft to firm
no lymphadenopathy, paresthesia, or facial palsy
Contrast-enhanced CT of the face showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space
Intracystic loculations with dense cystic content were noted, and there was erosion of the posterior buccal cortex without perforation of the maxilla
a clinical diagnosis of a nonspecific chronic abscess with buccal-space involvement

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a well-defined soft-tissue mass and cystic areas in the right buccal space, along with intracystic loculations and erosion of the posterior buccal cortex, is consistent with a staphylococcal buccal space abscess.

aliases: Tuberculous infection of the buccal space
concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a chronic, recurrent swelling in the buccal space, along with the presence of cystic areas and intracystic loculations, could be consistent with a tuberculous buccal space abscess.

The patient's presentation with a chronic, recurrent swelling in the buccal space, along with the presence of cystic areas and intracystic loculations, could be consistent with an actinomycotic buccal space abscess.

aliases: Dental infection with buccal space involvement
concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a well-defined soft-tissue mass and cystic areas in the right buccal space, along with intracystic loculations and erosion of the posterior buccal cortex, could be consistent with an odontogenic buccal space abscess.

concepts.preferred_label: Necrotizing fasciitis of the buccal space
concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a rapidly progressing, severe infection of the buccal space, along with the presence of cystic areas and intracystic loculations, could be consistent with necrotizing fasciitis of the buccal space.

rationales.F02: Reduced mouth opening suggests a space-occupying lesion in the buccal space.
rationales.F04: Absence of pain and fever makes an acute infection less likely.
rationales.F06: Gross facial asymmetry indicates a significant mass effect.
rationales.F10: Contrast-enhanced CT showing a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas is highly suggestive of an abscess.
rationales.F11: Intracystic loculations and erosion of the posterior buccal cortex are characteristic of a chronic abscess.
rationales.F12: A clinical diagnosis of a nonspecific chronic abscess with buccal-space involvement is highly suggestive of an abscess, making necrotizing fasciitis less likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: Recurring episodes over eight years and chronic nature of the abscess suggest a granulomatous infection, which is more consistent with tuberculosis than other options.
